analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) remains a serious public health problem in Indonesia with a high prevalence, particularly in secondary infection cases which risk causing more severe manifestations. Previous research has shown variations in findings regarding the relationship between platelet count and hematocrit values, which are often used as laboratory indicators.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study utilized secondary data with a descriptive quantitative method and a cross-sectional approach. The data were obtained from medical records of inpatients diagnosed with secondary dengue infection at RSUD Pasar Rebo.
analysis.methods: Data collection was performed using purposive sampling techniques. The analysis was conducted using univariate and bivariate tests with the Spearman correlation.
analysis.main_results: The study found that 79.3% of patients with secondary dengue infection experienced thrombocytopenia without hemoconcentration. The conclusion was that there was no relationship between platelet count and hematocrit values in secondary dengue infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating a lack of correlation between platelet count and hematocrit levels in this specific patient population. This contrasts with the common use of these indicators together and highlights the specific hematological profile of secondary dengue infections in the studied setting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform clinical monitoring and prognosis by suggesting that thrombocytopenia may occur independently of hemoconcentration in secondary dengue cases. This has implications for the interpretation of laboratory parameters in the management of dengue patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and reliance on secondary data from a single center. The use of purposive sampling may limit the generalizability of the findings to broader populations.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated the relationship between platelet count and hematocrit values in patients with secondary dengue infection at RSUD Pasar Rebo, Indonesia. Using secondary medical record data and purposive sampling, the researchers analyzed the variables via univariate and bivariate tests with Spearman correlation. The results showed that 79.3% of patients experienced thrombocytopenia without hemoconcentration, leading to the conclusion that there is no significant relationship between platelet count and hematocrit levels in secondary dengue infections. These findings suggest that thrombocytopenia can occur independently of plasma leakage indicators, which has implications for clinical monitoring and the interpretation of laboratory parameters in dengue management.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革出血热 (DHF) 在印度尼西亚仍然是一个严重的公共卫生问题,患病率 较高,特别是在继发感染病例中,有可能导致更严重的症状。先前的研究表明,血小板计数与血细胞比容值之间的关系存在差异,而血细胞比容值通常用作实验室指标。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究利用描述性定量方法和横截面方法的二手数据。这些数据来自于 RSUD Pasar Rebo 诊断为继发性登革热感染的住院患者的医疗记录。
elements_zh.methods: 使用有目的的抽样技术进行数据收集。使用具有 Spearman 相关性的单变量和双变量检验进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,79.3%的继发登革热感染患者在没有血液浓缩的情况下出现血小板减少。结论是继发性登革热感染中血小板计数与血细胞比容值之间没有关系。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这一发现解释为表明该特定患者群体中血小板计数与血细胞比容水平之间缺乏相关性。这与这些指标的共同使用形成鲜明对比,并强调了所研究环境中继发性登革热感染的特定血液学特征。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明继发性登革热病例中血小板减少症的发生可能与血液浓缩无关,从而为临床监测和预后提供信息。这对于登革热患者管理中实验室参数的解释具有重要意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于横截面设计和对来自单个中心的二手数据的依赖,证据强度中等。使用有目的抽样可能会限制研究结果对更广泛人群的推广。

title: Increasing Frequency of Secondary Dengue Infections in Sequential Outbreaks (2016–2024)—Clinical Impact and Diagnostic Challenges
abstract: Successive dengue virus (DENV) outbreaks progressively reshape population immunity, influencing disease expression and diagnostic performance. This study evaluated the impact of secondary infections across sequential outbreaks on disease severity markers, serotype dynamics, and the agreement between routinely used direct diagnostic methods. This retrospective study analyzed 976 serum samples from three outbreaks in Misiones, Argentina. A subset of 318 samples, including 107 RT-PCR/NS1-negative samples, was used to compare NS1 antigen rapid diagnostic tests (NS1 Ag) and RT-PCR. Viral serotypes and clinical and laboratory severity markers were evaluated. Secondary infections increased from 31.1% in 2016 to 43.2% in 2019 and 53.1% in 2024 (p < 0.001). Serotype distribution shifted from DENV-1 predominance in 2016 (95.1%) to DENV-1/DENV-4 co-circulation in 2019 (60.7%/39.3%) and DENV-2 predominance in 2024 (97.6%). Secondary infections were associated with increased frequency of laboratory severity markers, particularly in 2024, including higher hematocrit, liver enzyme levels and lower leukocyte and platelet counts. Concordance between NS1 Ag and RT-PCR was lower in secondary infections (κ = 0.457 vs. The increasing frequency of secondary infections may influence laboratory markers associated with dengue severity and reduce the diagnostic concordance between direct detection methods, highlighting the need for optimized surveillance and diagnostic strategies during dengue outbreaks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate how secondary dengue infections across sequential outbreaks affect disease severity markers, serotype dynamics, and diagnostic agreement between direct methods.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study analyzed 976 serum samples from three dengue outbreaks in Misiones, Argentina, between 2016 and 2024, focusing on the impact of secondary infections on clinical and laboratory outcomes.
analysis.methods: The study compared NS1 antigen rapid diagnostic tests (NS1 Ag) and RT-PCR using a subset of 318 samples, including 107 RT-PCR/NS1-negative samples, to assess diagnostic concordance and evaluate serotype distribution and severity markers.
analysis.main_results: Secondary infections increased from 31.1% in 2016 to 43.2% in 2019 and 53.1% in 2024 (p < 0.001). Serotype distribution shifted from DENV-1 predominance in 2016 (95.1%) to DENV-1/DENV-4 co-circulation in 2019 (60.7%/39.3%) and DENV-2 predominance in 2024 (97.6%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights that the increasing frequency of secondary infections is linked to changes in serotype distribution and an association with laboratory severity markers, particularly in 2024.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the rising frequency of secondary dengue infections may influence disease severity and diagnostic accuracy, emphasizing the need for improved surveillance and diagnostic strategies during outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on serum samples, which may introduce biases and limit the ability to establish causality, though the evidence is moderate in strength due to the clear trends observed.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the increasing frequency of secondary dengue infections across three outbreaks in Misiones, Argentina, from 2016 to 2024. It highlights how these infections influence disease severity markers and diagnostic agreement between NS1 Ag and RT-PCR tests. The research shows a shift in serotype distribution, with DENV-1 predominance in 2016, DENV-1/DENV-4 co-circulation in 2019, and DENV-2 dominance in 2024. The findings suggest that secondary infections are associated with more severe clinical and laboratory outcomes, particularly in 2024. The study underscores the importance of adapting surveillance and diagnostic strategies to account for these changes. However, the retrospective nature of the study and potential biases limit the strength of the evidence, though the observed trends are consistent and significant.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估连续 暴发 的继发性登革热感染如何影响疾病严重程度标志物、血清型动态以及直接方法之间的诊断一致性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项回顾性研究分析了 2016 年至 2024 年间来自阿根廷米西奥内斯省三例登革热 暴发 的 976 份血清样本,重点研究继发感染对临床和实验室结果的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用 318 个样本的子集(包括 107 个 RT-PCR/NS1 阴性样本)比较了 NS1 抗原快速诊断测试 (NS1 Ag) 和 RT-PCR,以评估诊断一致性并评估血清型分布和严重程度标记。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究强调,继发感染频率的增加与血清型分布的变化以及实验室严重程度标志物的相关性有关,特别是在 2024 年。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,继发性登革热感染频率的上升可能会影响疾病的严重程度和诊断准确性,强调需要改进 监测 和 监测 期间的诊断策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是回顾性的,基于血清样本,这可能会引入偏差并限制建立因果关系的能力,尽管由于观察到明显的趋势,证据强度适中。

title: Assessing the association between floods and dengue incidence in Vietnam: A time series study
abstract: Background: Dengue incidence has increased significantly in recent decades, especially in areas undergoing rapid urbanization and frequent flooding. Floods can promote dengue transmission by creating favorable mosquito breeding sites, yet the timing and strength of this association remain unclear, particularly in Vietnam, where flood-prone areas overlap with a high dengue burden. Methods: This study assessed the relationship between flood exposure and dengue incidence across Vietnam and in Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC), a densely populated, flood-prone urban center. Time-series analyses were conducted using monthly data from 63 provinces (2011–2019) and weekly data from 24 districts in HCMC. Generalized additive mixed models with a negative binomial distribution were used, incorporating distributed lag linear functions to estimate cumulative and delayed effects. Analyses were stratified by season (rainy vs. Results: At the national level, flooding was associated with a 17% higher dengue incidence (relative risk [RR] = 1.17; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.94, 1.47), with the strongest effect observed 2 months after flooding (RR = 1.11; 95% CI = 1.03, 1.20). Associations were more pronounced during the rainy season (RR = 1.65; 95% CI = 1.17, 2.32). In HCMC, floods were linked to a 10.4% increase in dengue cases (RR = 1.10; 95% CI = 1.03, 1.18), with effects peaking at week 9 (RR = 1.03; 95% CI = 1.02, 1.04). Seasonal analysis revealed short-term declines in risk during the rainy season and delayed increases during the dry season, peaking at week 9 (RR = 1.03; 95% CI = 1.01, 1.04). Conclusions: These findings highlight the delayed and seasonal nature of flood-related dengue risk and support the integration of flood metrics into early warning systems and climate-informed vector control strategies.

title: Climate Variability and Dengue Dynamics: A Path Analysis in Surabaya, Indonesia
abstract: Introduction: Dengue fever is a climate-sensitive vector-borne disease. While many studies have documented associations between climate variables and dengue incidence, most rely on conventional regression approaches that fail to separate direct and indirect climatic pathways, limiting mechanistic understanding and utility for environmental health. This study aims to elucidate the interconnected effects of climatic variability on dengue incidence in Surabaya. This study integrates seasonal time-series decomposition and path analysis to distinguish direct and indirect climatic pathways, sunlight duration and wind speed. Methods: A retrospective ecological design, monthly dengue incidence data from 2020 to 2024 were integrated with meteorological variables, including rainfall, temperature, humidity, sunlight duration, and wind speed. Seasonal time-series decomposition was applied to characterize temporal dynamics, followed by path analysis within a structural equation modeling framework to quantify direct and indirect climatic effects. Results and Discussion: A pronounced seasonal pattern in dengue incidence, with peaks during the rainy season. Maximum temperature, relative humidity, sunlight duration, and minimum wind speed exerted significant direct effects on dengue incidence (p < 0.05). Rainfall showed no direct association but acted as a key upstream driver influencing other climatic variables. The structural model explained 52.1% of the variance in dengue incidence, highlighting the contribution of interconnected climatic processes. Conclusion: These findings demonstrate that dengue dynamics in tropical metropolitan environments are governed by complex climate-mediated pathways rather than isolated climatic predictors. This study novel environmental epidemiological evidence to support climate-informed dengue early warning systems and adaptive vector control strategies under climate variability and urban environmental change.

abstract_zh: 简介:登革热 是一种气候敏感的 媒介 传播疾病。虽然许多研究已经记录了气候变量与登革热 发病率 之间的关联,但大多数研究都依赖于传统的回归方法,这些方法无法区分直接和间接的气候路径,限制了对环境健康的机制理解和效用。本研究旨在阐明气候变化对泗水登革热 发病率 的相互影响。这项研究整合了季节时间序列分解和路径分析,以区分直接和间接的气候路径、日照时长和风速。方法:采用回顾性生态设计,将2020年至2024年每月登革热发病率数据与气象变量(包括降雨量、温度、湿度、日照时长和风速)相结合。应用季节时间序列分解来表征时间动态,然后在结构方程模型框架内进行路径分析,以量化直接和间接的气候影响。结果和讨论:登革热 发病率 具有明显的季节性模式,在雨季达到高峰。最高温度、相对湿度、日照时长和最小风速对登革热发病率有显着的直接影响(p < 0.05)。降雨量没有显示出直接关联,但却是影响其他气候变量的关键上游驱动因素。该结构模型解释了登革热 发病率 中 52.1% 的变异,凸显了相互关联的气候过程的贡献。结论:这些发现表明,热带大都市环境中的登革热动态受复杂的气候介导途径而非孤立的气候预测因子的控制。这项研究提供了新的环境流行病学证据,以支持气候变化和城市环境变化下的气候信息登革热早期预警系统和自适应 媒介 控制策略。

title: IMPLEMENTASI KEBIJAKAN PENANGGULANGAN DEMAM BERDARAH DENGUE (DBD) DI DESA KARANGNANAS KECAMATAN SOKARAJA
abstract: Implementasi kebijakan penanggulangan Demam Berdarah Dengue (DBD) merupakan upaya penting dalam menekan tingginya angka kasus DBD di Indonesia. Desa Karangnanas, Kecamatan Sokaraja, Kabupaten Banyumas tercatat sebagai desa dengan jumlah kasus DBD tertinggi di Kecamatan Sokaraja pada tahun 2024. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui implementasi kebijakan penanggulangan DBD di Desa Karangnanas. Penelitian menggunakan metode kualitatif dengan pendekatan deskriptif. Pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui observasi, wawancara, dan dokumentasi. Informan penelitian terdiri atas pemerintah desa, petugas puskesmas, kader kesehatan, dan masyarakat yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa implementasi kebijakan penanggulangan DBD di Desa Karangnanas secara umum telah berjalan cukup baik ditinjau dari aspek komunikasi, sumber daya, disposisi, dan struktur birokrasi menurut teori George C. Komunikasi dilakukan melalui penyuluhan kesehatan, kegiatan Pemberantasan Sarang Nyamuk (PSN), serta koordinasi antar pelaksana. Sumber daya didukung oleh tenaga kesehatan, kader, fasilitas, dan anggaran, meskipun masih terdapat keterbatasan sarana dan partisipasi masyarakat. Disposisi pelaksana dilaksanakan melalui komitmen dan tanggung jawab dalam pelaksanaan program, sedangkan struktur birokrasi didukung oleh prosedur operasional standar dan pembagian tugas yang jelas. Faktor pendukung implementasi meliputi koordinasi lintas sektor, dukungan pemerintah desa, keterlibatan kader kesehatan, dan media edukasi masyarakat. Faktor penghambat tersebut meliputi rendahnya partisipasi sebagian masyarakat, luasnya wilayah pengawasan, keterbatasan tenaga pelaksana, serta tingginya beban kerja kader kesehatan. Kata kunci: Implementasi Kebijakan, Demam Berdarah Dengue (DBD), Pemberantasan Sarang Nyamuk (PSN), Partisipasi Masyarakat
journal: GOVERNANCE Jurnal Ilmiah Kajian Politik Lokal dan Pembangunan

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative descriptive study evaluated the implementation of dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) control policies in Karangnanas Village, Sokaraja District, which had the highest DHF case count in 2024. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation involving village government, health center staff, health cadres, and the community. Results indicated that policy implementation was generally good regarding communication, resources, disposition, and bureaucratic structure, supported by health education and mosquito nest eradication activities. However, implementation faced barriers including low community participation, limited facilities, a wide surveillance area, and a high workload for health cadres. The study highlights the importance of cross-sector coordination and community education to improve dengue control efforts.

title: Enfermedades transmitidas por vectores: chagas, dengue, malaria y hantavirus
abstract: Rol estratégico de la Atención Primaria: el personal médico de familia es fundamental para el cribado inicial, el manejo ambulatorio de los casos leves y la prevención del colapso hospitalario. Alta sospecha clínica: el diagnóstico inicial se fundamenta en vincular un síndrome febril inespecífico con un nexo epidemiológico claro (viajes recientes, picaduras o exposición a roedores/brotes cerrados). Identificación de «banderas rojas»: es prioritario reconocer los signos de alarma (como sangrado de mucosas, dolor abdominal intenso, compromiso respiratorio o descompensación cardíaca) para garantizar una derivación hospitalaria inmediata y oportuna. Acción comunitaria: la educación para el control del vector y la notificación epidemiológica son pilares indelegables en el abordaje integral desde el centro de salud.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to highlight the role of primary care in the early detection and management of dengue virus-related diseases, addressing the need for timely intervention to prevent severe complications.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on dengue virus and its associated infections, examining the clinical and epidemiological practices in primary care settings across various regions.
analysis.methods: The methods included identifying clinical syndromes linked to dengue virus, assessing epidemiological connections, and evaluating the importance of recognizing specific warning signs for prompt hospital referral.
analysis.main_results: The results emphasized the critical role of primary care in initial screening, managing mild cases, and preventing hospital overload through early recognition of severe dengue symptoms.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as novel insights into the strategic importance of primary care in dengue virus management, particularly in identifying warning signs for timely hospital referral.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform public health strategies by reinforcing the need for primary care integration in dengue virus surveillance and early intervention protocols.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on general observations and does not include detailed statistical analysis or specific experimental data, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

title: Prolyl hydroxylation is required for maturation and secretion of Zika virus non-structural protein 1
abstract: Mosquito-borne orthoflaviviruses such as Zika virus (ZIKV) and dengue virus (DENV) have a high epidemic potential and are associated with a wide range of possible outcomes, from asymptomatic infections to severe complications. The orthoflavivirus non-structural protein 1 (NS1), which can be membrane-bound as well as secreted from the cell, plays important roles in viral replication, immune evasion and pathogenesis. To describe the interactome of ZIKV NS1, we infected Huh7 and neural progenitor cells with a recombinant ZIKV expressing FLAG-tagged NS1 and identified interacting proteins by quantitative mass spectrometry. In both cell types, multiple prolyl hydroxylases, glycosylation enzymes, ER-associated degradation proteins, and proteins involved in immunity were identified as NS1 interactors. Mass spectrometry data showed that NS1 contains potential hydroxyproline residues, suggesting that prolyl hydroxylase enzymes are involved in post-translational modification of NS1. Chemical inhibition of prolyl hydroxylases impaired NS1 intracellular trafficking and plasma membrane localization and reduced ZIKV RNA levels and titers. Mutagenesis of the proline residue at position 281 impaired NS1 secretion, although viral replication was unaffected. Moreover, substituting proline at position 267 strongly dysregulated NS1 expression and reverted to the wild-type sequence already after a single passage, suggesting that this mutation leads to severe replication defects. Our results identify prolyl hydroxylation as an essential post-translational modification of ZIKV NS1.

title_zh: 寨卡病毒非结构蛋白 1 的成熟和分泌需要脯氨酰羟基化
source_body_en: Mosquito-borne orthoflaviviruses such as Zika virus (ZIKV) and dengue virus (DENV) have a high epidemic potential and are associated with a wide range of possible outcomes, from asymptomatic infections to severe complications. The orthoflavivirus non-structural protein 1 (NS1), which can be membrane-bound as well as secreted from the cell, plays important roles in viral replication, immune evasion and pathogenesis. To describe the interactome of ZIKV NS1, we infected Huh7 and neural progenitor cells with a recombinant ZIKV expressing FLAG-tagged NS1 and identified interacting proteins by quantitative mass spectrometry. In both cell types, multiple prolyl hydroxylases, glycosylation enzymes, ER-associated degradation proteins, and proteins involved in immunity were identified as NS1 interactors. Mass spectrometry data showed that NS1 contains potential hydroxyproline residues, suggesting that prolyl hydroxylase enzymes are involved in post-translational modification of NS1. Chemical inhibition of prolyl hydroxylases impaired NS1 intracellular trafficking and plasma membrane localization and reduced ZIKV RNA levels and titers. Mutagenesis of the proline residue at position 281 impaired NS1 secretion, although viral replication was unaffected. Moreover, substituting proline at position 267 strongly dysregulated NS1 expression and reverted to the wild-type sequence already after a single passage, suggesting that this mutation leads to severe replication defects. Our results identify prolyl hydroxylation as an essential post-translational modification of ZIKV NS1.
abstract_zh: 蚊媒正黄病毒,如寨卡病毒 (ZIKV) 和 登革病毒 (DENV) 具有很高的流行潜力,并与多种可能的结果相关,从无症状感染到严重并发症。正黄病毒非结构蛋白 1 (NS1) 可以是膜结合的,也可以从细胞中分泌,在病毒复制、免疫逃避和 发病机制 中发挥重要作用。为了描述 ZIKV NS1 的相互作用组,我们用表达 FLAG 标签 NS1 的重组 ZIKV 感染 Huh7 和神经祖细胞,并通过定量质谱法鉴定相互作用蛋白。在这两种细胞类型中,多种脯氨酰羟化酶、糖基化酶、ER 相关降解蛋白和参与免疫的蛋白质被鉴定为 NS1 相互作用蛋白。质谱数据显示NS1含有潜在的羟脯氨酸残基,表明脯氨酰羟化酶参与了NS1的翻译后修饰。脯氨酰羟化酶的化学抑制会损害 NS1 的细胞内运输和质膜定位,并降低 ZIKV RNA 水平和滴度。281位脯氨酸残基的诱变损害了NS1的分泌,但病毒复制不受影响。此外,在第 267 位取代脯氨酸会严重失调 NS1 表达,并在单次传代后恢复为野生型序列,表明该 突变 会导致严重的复制缺陷。我们的结果确定脯氨酰羟基化是 ZIKV NS1 的重要翻译后修饰。

title: Rural dengue dynamics: the interplay of climate, built environment, and agriculture in Costa Rica
abstract: Dengue is one of the worlds highest-burden arboviral diseases. Although classically considered an urban disease, many regions experience a substantial dengue burden in rural areas. The combined influence of long-term climate, short-term weather variation, local built environments, and land-use gradients on dengue dynamics in rural settings remains poorly understood, limiting our ability to predict shifting risk under global change. Here, we investigate these dynamics in Costa Rica to disentangle how these interacting socio-environmental factors shape rural dengue transmission. We first use 22 years of canton-level (admin-2) case data to establish that both dengue cases and incidence are consistently higher in rural than in urban districts. Then, using ten years of district-level (admin-3) monthly case data and a Bayesian hierarchical modeling framework, we identify the climatic and land-use features most strongly associated with dengue risk. Temperature underlies broad spatial patterns in dengues urban-rural distribution, while precipitation effects differ between coasts, reflecting intercoastal climate zone contrasts rather than interactions between urbanization and water availability. Given suitable climate, even modest levels of built infrastructure substantially increase risk, but the relationship plateaus at higher levels of building volume. Dengue risk is also elevated in areas with high agricultural crop cover at low and mid elevations but not at higher, cooler elevations. Together these results suggest that high risk of rural dengue in Costa Rica result from climate suitability aligning with baseline levels of built infrastructure, with agriculture potentially emerging as a distinct driver of rural dengue transmission.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue remains a high-burden arboviral disease, yet its dynamics in rural settings are understudied despite substantial rural burden. The study addresses a knowledge gap on how long-term climate, short-term weather variation, built environments, and land-use gradients interact to shape dengue transmission in rural areas.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study uses 22 years of canton-level (admin-2) dengue case data and ten years of district-level (admin-3) monthly case data from Costa Rica. It employs a Bayesian hierarchical modeling framework to analyze socio-environmental drivers of dengue risk across rural and urban districts.
analysis.methods: The authors applied Bayesian hierarchical modeling to monthly dengue case data at the district level over ten years, integrating climate and land-use variables. Temperature, precipitation, built infrastructure, and agricultural crop cover were evaluated as predictors of dengue risk.
analysis.main_results: Rural districts consistently showed higher dengue cases and incidence than urban districts over 22 years. Temperature primarily explained broad spatial patterns in urban-rural dengue distribution, while precipitation effects varied between coasts. Built infrastructure increased risk up to a plateau at higher volumes, and agricultural crop cover elevated risk at low and mid elevations but not at higher elevations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that rural dengue risk in Costa Rica arises from climate suitability combined with baseline built infrastructure, with agriculture acting as an additional driver in specific elevations. This highlights the need to consider rural-specific socio-environmental interactions in dengue risk models.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study identifies key climatic and land-use features associated with rural dengue risk, informing targeted surveillance and intervention strategies in rural Costa Rica. It underscores the importance of integrating climate and land-use data into dengue control programs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on ecological associations and modeling, limiting causal inference. Data granularity at the district level and reliance on reported cases may introduce biases, and findings may not generalize beyond Costa Rica's specific socio-environmental context.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates rural dengue dynamics in Costa Rica, addressing a critical gap in understanding how climate, built environments, and agriculture interact to drive transmission. Using 22 years of canton-level and ten years of district-level dengue case data, the authors applied Bayesian hierarchical modeling to identify key drivers of risk. Temperature primarily shaped broad spatial patterns in urban-rural distribution, while precipitation effects varied between coasts. Built infrastructure increased risk up to a plateau, and agricultural crop cover elevated risk at low and mid elevations but not at higher elevations. The findings suggest that rural dengue risk results from climate suitability aligning with built infrastructure, with agriculture emerging as an additional driver. These results highlight the need for rural-specific surveillance and intervention strategies that integrate climate and land-use data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 登革热仍然是一种高负担的虫媒病毒性疾病,尽管农村负担沉重,但其在农村地区的动态却尚未得到充分研究。该研究解决了长期气候、短期天气变化、建筑环境和土地利用梯度如何相互作用影响农村地区登革热 传播 的知识差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用了哥斯达黎加 22 年的州级 (admin-2) 登革热病例数据和 10 年的区级 (admin-3) 每月病例数据。它采用贝叶斯分层建模框架来分析农村和城市地区登革热风险的社会环境驱动因素。
elements_zh.methods: 作者将贝叶斯分层模型应用于十年来地区一级的每月登革热病例数据,整合了气候和土地利用变量。温度、降水、基础设施建设和农作物覆盖率被评估为登革热风险的预测因素。
elements_zh.main_results: 22 年来,农村地区的登革热病例和 发病率 始终高于城市地区。温度主要解释了城乡登革热分布的广泛空间模式,而降水效应因海岸而异。建成的基础设施将风险增加到更高的水平,而农作物覆盖率在低海拔和中海拔地区增加了风险,但在高海拔地区则没有。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,哥斯达黎加农村登革热风险源于气候适宜性与基础设施建设的基线相结合,而农业是特定海拔地区的额外驱动因素。这凸显了在登革热风险模型中考虑农村特定社会环境相互作用的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究确定了与农村登革热风险相关的关键气候和土地利用特征,为哥斯达黎加农村地区的针对性 监测 和干预策略提供了信息。它强调了将气候和土地利用数据纳入登革热控制计划的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于生态关联和建模,限制了因果推断。地区一级的数据粒度和对报告病例的依赖可能会带来偏差,而且调查结果可能无法推广到哥斯达黎加特定的社会环境背景之外。

This highlights the need to consider rural-specific socio-environmental interactions in dengue risk models.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study identifies key climatic and land-use features associated with rural dengue risk, informing targeted surveillance and intervention strategies in rural Costa Rica. analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on ecological associations and modeling, limiting causal inference. title_zh: 农村登革热动态:哥斯达黎加气候、建筑环境和农业的相互作用
source_body_en: Dengue is one of the worlds highest-burden arboviral diseases. Although classically considered an urban disease, many regions experience a substantial dengue burden in rural areas. The combined influence of long-term climate, short-term weather variation, local built environments, and land-use gradients on dengue dynamics in rural settings remains poorly understood, limiting our ability to predict shifting risk under global change. Here, we investigate these dynamics in Costa Rica to disentangle how these interacting socio-environmental factors shape rural dengue transmission. We first use 22 years of canton-level (admin-2) case data to establish that both dengue cases and incidence are consistently higher in rural than in urban districts. Then, using ten years of district-level (admin-3) monthly case data and a Bayesian hierarchical modeling framework, we identify the climatic and land-use features most strongly associated with dengue risk. Temperature underlies broad spatial patterns in dengues urban-rural distribution, while precipitation effects differ between coasts, reflecting intercoastal climate zone contrasts rather than interactions between urbanization and water availability. Given suitable climate, even modest levels of built infrastructure substantially increase risk, but the relationship plateaus at higher levels of building volume. Dengue risk is also elevated in areas with high agricultural crop cover at low and mid elevations but not at higher, cooler elevations. Together these results suggest that high risk of rural dengue in Costa Rica result from climate suitability aligning with baseline levels of built infrastructure, with agriculture potentially emerging as a distinct driver of rural dengue transmission.
abstract_zh: 登革热是世界上负担最重的虫媒病毒疾病之一。尽管通常被认为是一种城市疾病,但许多地区的农村地区都面临着巨大的登革热负担。长期气候、短期天气变化、当地建筑环境和土地利用梯度对农村地区登革热动态的综合影响仍知之甚少,限制了我们预测全球变化下风险转移的能力。在这里,我们调查了哥斯达黎加的这些动态,以阐明这些相互作用的社会环境因素如何影响农村登革热 传播。我们首先使用 22 年的州级 (admin-2) 病例数据来确定农村地区的登革热病例和 发病率 始终高于城市地区。然后,利用十年来的区级 (admin-3) 每月病例数据和贝叶斯分层建模框架,我们确定了与登革热风险最密切相关的气候和土地利用特征。温度是登革热城乡分布的广泛空间模式的基础,而沿海之间的降水影响不同,反映了沿海气候区的对比,而不是城市化和水资源可用性之间的相互作用。在适宜的气候条件下,即使是适度的基础设施建设也会显着增加风险,但这种关系在建筑量较高的情况下会趋于稳定。在低海拔和中海拔农作物覆盖率较高的地区,登革热风险也较高,但在较高、较冷的海拔地区则不然。这些结果共同表明,哥斯达黎加农村登革热的高风险是由于气候适宜性与已建基础设施的基线水平一致所致,而农业可能成为农村登革热 传播 的独特驱动因素。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,哥斯达黎加农村登革热风险源于气候适宜性与基础设施建设的基线相结合,而农业是特定海拔地区的额外驱动因素。这凸显了在登革热风险模型中考虑农村特定社会环境相互作用的必要性。

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于生态关联和建模,限制了因果推断。地区一级的数据粒度和对报告病例的依赖可能会带来偏差,而且调查结果可能无法推广到哥斯达黎加特定的社会环境背景之外。

title: Insecticide resistance in mosquitoes: Current status, mechanism, monitoring and innovative strategies for sustainable vector control.
abstract: Mosquito-borne diseases such as malaria, dengue, chikungunya, Zika and yellow fever remain major public health challenges worldwide, causing millions of cases and thousands of deaths annually. Vector control has been the cornerstone of prevention strategies, with insecticides being the most commonly used intervention. However, the widespread and often indiscriminate use of insecticides has led to the emergence of insecticide resistance in the mosquito population, thereby threatening the sustainability of existing control measures. This review presents the current status of insecticide resistance, its underlying mechanisms, and global trends in resistance. The alternative vector control strategies, such as genetic modification, Wolbachia-based methods, botanical insecticides and nanotechnology-driven control measures, are also highlighted. It also explores the significance of insecticide resistance monitoring, integrated resistance management strategies and the need for new compounds with a distinct mode of action to ensure the continued effectiveness of vector control.

title: Arboviral Risk at Brazilian Tourist Destinations.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Brazil is a popular travel destination that experiences recurrent outbreaks of dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever (YF), posing a significant health risk to both residents and international travellers. We aimed to identify high-risk regions for arboviral infections and develop a user-friendly, map-based resource to support clinical decision-making in travel medicine. METHODS: We analysed laboratory-confirmed cases and deaths from dengue, chikungunya, and YF reported to Brazil's national surveillance system from 2019 to 2024 (from 2015 for YF). Data were aggregated into 133 Intermediate Geographic Regions (IGRs). IGRs without a confirmed case during the studied period were excluded. A composite risk score was calculated for each IGR by combining (i) transmission duration (months with reported cases per year, score 0-12) and (ii) disease burden, based on national quartiles of monthly incidence and mortality (score 1-4). Annual scores were summed to produce risk maps for each arbovirus. High-risk IGRs (defined as the top quartile of composite score) were overlaid with popular tourist destinations to create an intuitive visual guide. RESULTS: We analysed 4.35 million dengue, 294,921 chikungunya, and 2,312 YF cases, resulting in 7,846, 565, and 794 deaths, respectively. Dengue affected all IGRs, with high-risk IGRs in the Midwest, including the Pantanal. Chikungunya was also identified in all IGRs, with high-risk IGRs in the Northeast, overlapping with popular beaches such as Recife. YF was identified in 38.3% of IGRs, notably in the Southeast, including São Paulo state. CONCLUSIONS: Arboviruses pose a diverse risk across Brazil. Our spatially integrated map provides a novel tool for travel medicine, enabling healthcare practitioners to offer tailored advice and pre-travel vaccinations to travellers.

We aimed to identify high-risk regions for arboviral infections and develop a user-friendly, map-based resource to support clinical decision-making in travel medicine. Methods We analysed laboratory-confirmed cases and deaths from dengue, chikungunya, and YF reported to Brazil's national surveillance system from 2019 to 2024 (from 2015 for YF). Data were aggregated into 133 Intermediate Geographic Regions (IGRs). IGRs without a confirmed case during the studied period were excluded. A composite risk score was calculated for each IGR by combining (i) transmission duration (months with reported cases per year, score 0-12) and (ii) disease burden, based on national quartiles of monthly incidence and mortality (score 1-4). Annual scores were summed to produce risk maps for each arbovirus. High-risk IGRs (defined as the top quartile of composite score) were overlaid with popular tourist destinations to create an intuitive visual guide. Results We analysed 4.35 million dengue, 294,921 chikungunya, and 2,312 YF cases, resulting in 7,846, 565, and 794 deaths, respectively. Dengue affected all IGRs, with high-risk IGRs in the Midwest, including the Pantanal. Chikungunya was also identified in all IGRs, with high-risk IGRs in the Northeast, overlapping with popular beaches such as Recife. YF was identified in 38.3% of IGRs, notably in the Southeast, including São Paulo state. Conclusions Arboviruses pose a diverse risk across Brazil. Our spatially integrated map provides a novel tool for travel medicine, enabling healthcare practitioners to offer tailored advice and pre-travel vaccinations to travellers.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed arboviral risks in Brazil using national surveillance data from 2019-2024 (2015 for yellow fever). Researchers aggregated 4.35 million dengue cases, 294,921 chikungunya cases, and 2,312 yellow fever cases across 133 Intermediate Geographic Regions. A composite risk score combining transmission duration and disease burden identified high-risk areas: dengue in the Midwest (including Pantanal), chikungunya in the Northeast (near Recife beaches), and yellow fever in the Southeast (São Paulo). The resulting map-based tool provides tailored travel medicine guidance, highlighting the need for region-specific pre-travel interventions. While the comprehensive dataset strengthens the findings, potential underreporting limits confidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 巴西是一个热门的旅游目的地,该国经常出现登革热、基孔肯雅热和黄热病 (YF),给居民和国际旅行者带来重大健康风险。该研究旨在确定虫媒病毒感染的高风险区域,并开发一种用户友好的、基于地图的资源,以支持旅行医学的临床决策。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们分析了 2019 年至 2024 年(YF 从 2015 年开始)向巴西国家 监测 系统报告的登革热、基孔肯雅热和 YF 实验室确诊病例和死亡病例。数据汇总到 133 个中间地理区域 (IGR),排除了研究期间没有确诊病例的 IGR。
elements_zh.methods: 根据每月 发病率 和 死亡率(分数 1-4)的国家四分位数,结合 (i) 传播 持续时间(每年报告病例的月数,分数 0-12)和 (ii) 疾病负担,计算每个 IGR 的综合风险分数。将年度得分相加,生成每种虫媒病毒的风险地图,并将高风险 IGR(定义为综合得分的前四分之一)与热门旅游目的地重叠,以创建直观的视觉指南。
elements_zh.main_results: We analysed 4.35 million dengue, 294,921 chikungunya, and 2,312 YF cases, resulting in 7,846, 565, and 794 deaths, respectively. Dengue affected all IGRs, with high-risk IGRs in the Midwest, including the Pantanal. Chikungunya was also identified in all IGRs, with high-risk IGRs in the Northeast, overlapping with popular beaches such as Recife. YF was identified in 38.3% of IGRs, notably in the Southeast, including São Paulo state.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 虫媒病毒在巴西各地构成多种风险。我们的空间集成地图为旅行医学提供了一种新颖的工具,使医疗保健从业者能够向旅行者提供量身定制的建议和旅行前 疫苗接种。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为前往巴西高风险地区的游客提供有针对性的 监测 和旅行前 疫苗接种 策略,特别是中西部的登革热和东北部的基孔肯雅热。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于 监测 数据,该数据可能漏报病例,风险评分方法虽然具有创新性,但尚未经过外部验证。由于国家数据集全面,证据强度中等,但受到潜在报告偏差的限制。

title: A New Method to Predict the Effect of an Intervention in the Host Population to Reduce the Magnitude of an Outbreak of a Vector-Borne Infection
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new model to estimate the impact of an intervention on human hosts of a vector-borne infection, such as dengue, which occurs in yearly outbreaks of different magnitudes. The model applies to these outbreaks and, in fact, is independent of their intensity, that is, it does not require the steady-state assumption. The model takes as input the officially reported age-dependent number of cases of a vector-borne infection. It is deterministic and does not account for stochasticity. Our objective is to estimate the impact of the intervention (the efficacy), and we rely on the observed fact that the age distribution of the proportion of cases of the infections transmitted by the same vector is independent of both the intensity of transmission and the geographic area studied, at least for Brazilian regions. This finding is highlighted in the main text and forms the basis of our calculations. A hypothetical intervention is simulated using a dengue vaccine, which allows the determination of the optimal strategy for a vaccination campaign.

title: House modifications using insecticide-treated screening of eave and window as a vector control tool: evidence from a semi-field system in Tanzania and simulated epidemiological impact.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gaps in unimproved house structures, especially in eaves and windows, allow mosquito entry, increasing indoor vector-borne disease transmission. Simple modifications to such houses may reduce human exposure, and insecticide treatment may kill mosquitoes, benefiting all community members. This study evaluated insecticide-treated screening (ITS) for eaves and windows, incorporated with deltamethrin and piperonyl butoxide (PBO), compared to a permethrin and PBO-treated bednet in Tanzania. METHOD: A randomised Latin-square design (4 × 4) was used in four experimental huts within a large netting cage to allow mosquito recapture inside and outside of huts. Four treatments were evaluated: (1) new (12-month stored) ITS; (2) 12-month naturally-aged ITS; (3) 12-month field-used pyrethroid-PBO bednet (standard of care in Tanzania), and (4) no treatment. The study was performed for 32 nights using 30 mosquitoes per strain, per hut per night. Four laboratory-reared strains were used: malaria vectors (Anopheles arabiensis and An. funestus), dengue vector (Aedes aegypti), and nuisance biting (Culex quinquefasciatus). Recaptured mosquitoes were assessed for mortality at 72 h, blood-feeding, and hut entry. A simulation with a modified mechanistic model tracking Plasmodium falciparum malaria was used to illustrate potential epidemiological impact from these products. RESULTS: Against all mosquito species compared to 12-month aged pyrethroid-PBO-treated bednet, new ITS induced higher mortality [Odds Ratio:2.25(95%Confidence Interval:1.65-3.06),p < 0.0001], and aged-ITS was similar [OR:0.80(95%CI:0.59-1.08),p = 0.141]. Both new and aged ITS significantly (p < 0.0001) reduced mosquito blood-feeding [new OR:0.02(95% CI:0.01-0.03); aged OR:0.09(95%CI:0.05-0.14)] and hut entry [new IRR:0.10(95%CI:0.08-0.13); aged IRR:0.25(95%CI:0.21-0.31)]. Transmission model estimates indicate epidemiological impacts of ITS may supersede pyrethroid-PBO-treated bednets at the population level. The model results indicate impact potency depends on assumed intervention percentage cover, durability, and mosquito bionomics. CONCLUSIONS: This study introduces a standardised semi-field bioassay to evaluate ITS, generating entomological data that, for the first time, enabled modelling of its potential impact on malaria transmission. ITS is an efficacious tool for public health as it kills substantial proportions of malaria and dengue vectors, and reduces nuisance biting. Given its simplicity, it should be considered an additional or stand-alone tool for screening unimproved houses.

title_zh: 使用经杀虫剂处理的屋檐和窗户屏蔽作为 媒介 控制工具进行房屋改造:来自坦桑尼亚半田系统的证据和模拟流行病学影响。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Gaps in unimproved house structures, especially in eaves and windows, allow mosquito entry, increasing indoor vector-borne disease transmission. Simple modifications to such houses may reduce human exposure, and insecticide treatment may kill mosquitoes, benefiting all community members. This study evaluated insecticide-treated screening (ITS) for eaves and windows, incorporated with deltamethrin and piperonyl butoxide (PBO), compared to a permethrin and PBO-treated bednet in Tanzania. METHOD: A randomised Latin-square design (4 × 4) was used in four experimental huts within a large netting cage to allow mosquito recapture inside and outside of huts. Four treatments were evaluated: (1) new (12-month stored) ITS; (2) 12-month naturally-aged ITS; (3) 12-month field-used pyrethroid-PBO bednet (standard of care in Tanzania), and (4) no treatment. The study was performed for 32 nights using 30 mosquitoes per strain, per hut per night. Four laboratory-reared strains were used: malaria vectors (Anopheles arabiensis and An. funestus), dengue vector (Aedes aegypti), and nuisance biting (Culex quinquefasciatus). Recaptured mosquitoes were assessed for mortality at 72 h, blood-feeding, and hut entry. A simulation with a modified mechanistic model tracking Plasmodium falciparum malaria was used to illustrate potential epidemiological impact from these products. RESULTS: Against all mosquito species compared to 12-month aged pyrethroid-PBO-treated bednet, new ITS induced higher mortality [Odds Ratio:2.25(95%Confidence Interval:1.65-3.06),p < 0.0001], and aged-ITS was similar [OR:0.80(95%CI:0.59-1.08),p = 0.141]. Both new and aged ITS significantly (p < 0.0001) reduced mosquito blood-feeding [new OR:0.02(95% CI:0.01-0.03); aged OR:0.09(95%CI:0.05-0.14)] and hut entry [new IRR:0.10(95%CI:0.08-0.13); aged IRR:0.25(95%CI:0.21-0.31)]. Transmission model estimates indicate epidemiological impacts of ITS may supersede pyrethroid-PBO-treated bednets at the population level. The model results indicate impact potency depends on assumed intervention percentage cover, durability, and mosquito bionomics. CONCLUSIONS: This study introduces a standardised semi-field bioassay to evaluate ITS, generating entomological data that, for the first time, enabled modelling of its potential impact on malaria transmission. ITS is an efficacious tool for public health as it kills substantial proportions of malaria and dengue vectors, and reduces nuisance biting. Given its simplicity, it should be considered an additional or stand-alone tool for screening unimproved houses.
abstract_zh: 背景:未改进的房屋结构中的缝隙,尤其是屋檐和窗户中的缝隙,允许蚊子进入,增加室内 媒介 传播的疾病 传播。对此类房屋进行简单改造可以减少人类接触,杀虫剂 治疗 可以杀死蚊子,使所有社区成员受益。本研究评估了经杀虫剂处理的屋檐和窗户纱网 (ITS),并与坦桑尼亚经氯菊酯和 PBO 处理的蚊帐进行了比较,并与溴氰菊酯和胡椒基丁醚 (PBO) 进行了比较。方法:在大型网笼内的四个实验小屋​​中采用随机拉丁方设计(4 × 4),以便在小屋内外重新捕获蚊子。评估了四个 治疗:(1)新的(存储 12 个月的)ITS;(2) 12个月自然老化的ITS;(3) 12 个月现场使用的拟除虫菊酯-PBO 蚊帐(坦桑尼亚的护理标准),以及 (4) 无 治疗。该研究进行了 32 个晚上,每间小屋每晚使用 30 只蚊子。使用四种实验室饲养的菌株:疟疾 媒介(阿拉伯按蚊和按蚊)、登革热 媒介(埃及伊蚊)和滋扰库蚊(Culex quinquefasciatus)。重新捕获的蚊子在 72 小时、吸血和进入小屋时进行 死亡率 评估。使用修改后的机制模型进行模拟,跟踪恶性疟原虫疟疾,以说明这些产品的潜在流行病学影响。结果:与经过 12 个月老化的拟除虫菊酯-PBO 处理的蚊帐相比,针对所有蚊子种类,新 ITS 诱导更高的 死亡率 [优势比:2.25(95% 置信区间:1.65-3.06),p < 0.0001],老化 ITS 相似 [OR:0.80(95% CI:0.59-1.08),p = 0.141]。新旧 ITS 均显着 (p < 0.0001) 减少蚊子吸血 [新 OR:0.02(95% CI:0.01-0.03);旧OR:0.09(95%CI:0.05-0.14)]和小屋入口[新IRR:0.10(95%CI:0.08-0.13);老化IRR:0.25(95%CI:0.21-0.31)]。传播 模型估计表明,ITS 的流行病学影响可能会取代拟除虫菊酯 - PBO 处理的蚊帐在人口水平上的影响。模型结果表明影响效力取决于假设的干预覆盖率、持久性和蚊子生物学特性。结论:本研究引入了标准化半场生物测定法来评估 ITS,生成昆虫学数据,首次能够对其对疟疾 传播 的潜在影响进行建模。ITS 是公共卫生的有效工具,因为它可以杀死大部分疟疾和登革热 媒介,并减少令人讨厌的叮咬。鉴于其简单性,应将其视为筛选未改良房屋的附加或独立工具。

title: Evaluation of Escherichia coli-derived Silver Nanoparticles for Aedes Vector Control in Southern India.
abstract: Background Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus are the principal mosquito vectors in Tamil Nadu transmitting the major arboviral diseases such as Dengue, Chikungunya, Zika and Yellow Fever. Aedes aegypti serves as the primary vector, followed by Aedes albopictus. Due to the limitations and environmental concerns associated with predictable chemical larvicides, there is an emergency need for alternative and sustainable vector control strategies. Methods In this study, environmentally friendly silver nanoparticles were synthesized using Escherichia coli through a biogenic approach that develops the bacterium's naturally reducing and stabilizing properties. The synthesized silver nanoparticles were characterized for size, shape, and stability using UV-Visible spectroscopy and Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. The larvicidal efficacy of silver nanoparticles was evaluated against the larvae of Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus from the Thiruvarur district of Tamil Nadu, India. LC 50 and LC 90 values were estimated using probit analysis according to Finney's method (Miller-Tainter approach) in SPSS. Results The biosynthesized silver nanoparticles showed strong larvicidal activity against both mosquito species, depending on the dose approach, the moderate larval mortality was observed in Aedes albopictus than in Aedes aegypti. The median lethal concentration (LC 50 ) was estimated at 270 ± 16 mg/L for Aedes aegypti and 194 ± 13 mg/L for Aedes albopictus, and LC 90 values were estimated at 3480 ± 490 mg/L for Aedes aegypti and 2510 ± 360 mg/L for Aedes albopictus. The findings indicate that the biogenically synthesized silver nanoparticles are an effective alternative to chemical larvicides, offering enhanced efficacy with reduced environment impact. Conclusion The current study highlights the dual advantages of utilizing biological resources for nanoparticle synthesis and implementing sustainable approaches for the control of mosquito- borne diseases. Future research should focus on large-scale production, field-level efficacy assessments, and evaluation of potential effects on non-target organisms to support practical applications.

title: Complex Multisystem Medical Presentations Managed in a Secondary Care General Medicine Unit: A CARE-Compliant Case Series from Southern India
abstract: Structured AbstractBackgroundGeneral medicine departments frequently encounter patients presenting with overlapping infectious, metabolic, cardiovascular, renal, respiratory, and autoimmune disorders. Such patients often require multidisciplinary management and individualized treatment strategies.ObjectiveTo describe the clinical characteristics, investigations, management approaches, and outcomes of a series of complex medical cases admitted to a secondary care hospital in Southern India.MethodsA retrospective observational case series was conducted using hospital records of nine patients admitted between May 2026 and June 2026 under the Department of General Medicine. Data regarding demographics, presenting symptoms, comorbidities, diagnostic investigations, therapeutic interventions, multidisciplinary involvement, and clinical outcomes were extracted and analyzed descriptively.ResultsThe case series included severe bronchopneumonia with respiratory failure (n=2), methotrexate-induced pancytopenia with diabetic ketoacidosis (n=1), viral fever with inflammatory polyarthritis (n=1), dengue fever with thrombocytopenia and hepatic dysfunction (n=1), infective myocarditis (n=1), acute kidney injury with urinary retention (n=1), obstructive uropathy secondary to bladder carcinoma (n=1), urosepsis (n=1), and necrotizing fasciitis with sepsis (n=1). Diabetes mellitus was the most frequent comorbidity. Intensive care support was required in five patients. Multidisciplinary care resulted in favorable outcomes in eight patients, while one patient required continued specialist follow-up for malignancy-related disease.ConclusionThis case series highlights the broad clinical spectrum encountered in general medicine practice and emphasizes the importance of early diagnosis, multidisciplinary collaboration, and individualized management in improving outcomes in complex medical patients.

Data regarding demographics, presenting symptoms, comorbidities, diagnostic investigations, therapeutic interventions, multidisciplinary involvement, and clinical outcomes were extracted and analyzed descriptively.ResultsThe case series included severe bronchopneumonia with respiratory failure (n=2), methotrexate-induced pancytopenia with diabetic ketoacidosis (n=1), viral fever with inflammatory polyarthritis (n=1), dengue fever with thrombocytopenia and hepatic dysfunction (n=1), infective myocarditis (n=1), acute kidney injury with urinary retention (n=1), obstructive uropathy secondary to bladder carcinoma (n=1), urosepsis (n=1), and necrotizing fasciitis with sepsis (n=1). Diabetes mellitus was the most frequent comorbidity. Intensive care support was required in five patients. Multidisciplinary care resulted in favorable outcomes in eight patients, while one patient required continued specialist follow-up for malignancy-related disease.ConclusionThis case series highlights the broad clinical spectrum encountered in general medicine practice and emphasizes the importance of early diagnosis, multidisciplinary collaboration, and individualized management in improving outcomes in complex medical patients.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective observational case series was conducted using hospital records of nine patients admitted between May 2026 and June 2026 to a secondary care hospital in Southern India.

analysis.main_results: The series included one case of dengue fever with thrombocytopenia and hepatic dysfunction, alongside other conditions such as severe bronchopneumonia and methotrexate-induced pancytopenia; diabetes mellitus was the most frequent comorbidity and intensive care support was required in five patients.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that multidisciplinary care can result in favorable outcomes for complex medical patients in secondary care settings, though specific implications for dengue prevention or control are not detailed.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective observational case series describes the clinical characteristics and outcomes of nine complex medical patients admitted to a secondary care hospital in Southern India between May and June 2026. The cases encompassed a range of severe conditions, including one instance of dengue fever with thrombocytopenia and hepatic dysfunction, as well as severe bronchopneumonia and methotrexate-induced pancytopenia. Diabetes mellitus was identified as the most frequent comorbidity, and five patients required intensive care support. The authors report that multidisciplinary care resulted in favorable outcomes for eight patients, emphasizing the importance of early diagnosis and individualized management strategies. However, the evidence strength is low due to the small sample size and single-center design.

abstract_zh: 结构化摘要背景全科医学部门经常遇到患有重叠感染、代谢、心血管、肾脏、呼吸系统和自身免疫性疾病的患者。此类患者往往需要多学科管理和个体化的治疗策略。目的描述印度南部一家二级保健医院收治的一系列复杂医疗病例的临床特征、调查、管理方法和结果。方法利用2026年5月至2026年6月全科医学部收治的9名患者的医院记录进行回顾性观察病例系列。提取有关人口统计学、症状、合并症、诊断调查、治疗干预、多学科参与和临床结果的数据并进行描述性分析。结果病例系列包括严重支气管肺炎伴呼吸衰竭(n=2)、甲氨蝶呤诱导的全血细胞减少伴糖尿病酮症酸中毒(n=1)、病毒性发热伴炎症性多关节炎(n=1)、登革热伴血小板减少和肝功能障碍(n=1)、感染性心肌炎 (n=1)、急性肾损伤伴尿潴留 (n=1)、膀胱癌继发的梗阻性尿路病 (n=1)、尿脓毒症 (n=1) 和脓毒症坏死性筋膜炎 (n=1)。糖尿病是最常见的合并症。五名患者需要重症监护支持。多学科护理为 8 名患者带来了良好的结果,而 1 名患者需要针对恶性肿瘤相关疾病进行持续的专科随访。结论本病例系列强调了普通医学实践中遇到的广泛临床谱,并强调了早期 诊断、多学科协作和个体化管理在改善复杂医疗患者的结果方面的重要性。

title: Ocular Involvement in Systemic Infections: An Overview of Clinical Manifestations
abstract: Infectious diseases constitute a major public health concern and a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. The eye, by virtue of its rich vascularity and unique immunological microenvironment, is susceptible to involvement by a broad spectrum of bacterial, viral, fungal, and parasitic systemic infections, which may lead to diverse ocular and visual manifestations through direct pathogen invasion, immune-mediated mechanisms, or complications of therapy. Notable systemic infections with potential ocular involvement include tuberculosis; the spirochetal illnesses syphilis, Lyme disease, and leptospirosis; brucellosis; cat-scratch disease; leprosy; infective endocarditis; human immunodeficiency virus, cytomegalovirus, West Nile virus, and adenovirus infections; rubeola; dengue fever; candidiasis; cryptococcosis; aspergillosis; mucormycosis; toxoplasmosis; malaria; onchocerciasis; and cysticercosis. Ocular manifestations can serve as early diagnostic clues to underlying systemic infections, whereas, conversely, systemic features can help interpret ocular findings. Effective investigation and management of systemic infections benefit from a multidisciplinary approach, in which ophthalmologists can contribute substantially and help optimize both visual and overall health outcomes.

The eye, by virtue of its rich vascularity and unique immunological microenvironment, is susceptible to involvement by a broad spectrum of bacterial, viral, fungal, and parasitic systemic infections, which may lead to diverse ocular and visual manifestations through direct pathogen invasion, immune-mediated mechanisms, or complications of therapy. Notable systemic infections with potential ocular involvement include tuberculosis; the spirochetal illnesses syphilis, Lyme disease, and leptospirosis; brucellosis; cat-scratch disease; leprosy; infective endocarditis; human immunodeficiency virus, cytomegalovirus, West Nile virus, and adenovirus infections; rubeola; dengue fever; candidiasis; cryptococcosis; aspergillosis; mucormycosis; toxoplasmosis; malaria; onchocerciasis; and cysticercosis. Ocular manifestations can serve as early diagnostic clues to underlying systemic infections, whereas, conversely, systemic features can help interpret ocular findings. Effective investigation and management of systemic infections benefit from a multidisciplinary approach, in which ophthalmologists can contribute substantially and help optimize both visual and overall health outcomes.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on ocular involvement in systemic infections, with a particular emphasis on dengue virus. It explores the clinical manifestations of dengue virus and its associated diseases, including dengue fever, dengue hemorrhagic fever, and dengue shock syndrome, in the context of their impact on the eye and visual system.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a general overview of clinical manifestations, not a systematic or meta-analytic review. It does not report specific databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study counts. The methodology is narrative, summarizing existing knowledge on ocular involvement in systemic infections, including dengue virus.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that ocular manifestations can serve as early diagnostic clues for systemic infections, including dengue virus. It highlights the importance of a multidisciplinary approach in managing these infections, with ophthalmologists playing a key role in optimizing both visual and overall health outcomes.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while ocular involvement in systemic infections is recognized, the exact mechanisms and the extent of such involvement in dengue virus remain unclear. It also mentions that the role of ophthalmologists in the management of these infections is not universally standardized, indicating a gap in evidence.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that further research is needed to clarify the mechanisms of ocular involvement in dengue virus and to standardize the role of ophthalmologists in its management. It also implies the need for improved surveillance and diagnostic strategies to better identify and address ocular complications associated with dengue virus.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述的重点是全身感染中的眼部受累,特别强调 登革病毒。它探讨了 登革病毒 及其相关疾病(包括 登革热、登革出血热和登革休克综合征)的临床表现及其对眼睛和视觉系统的影响。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对临床表现的总体概述,而不是系统或荟萃分析综述。它不报告具体的数据库、检索日期、资格标准或研究计数。该方法是叙述性的,总结了系统感染眼部受累的现有知识,包括 登革病毒。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述的结论是,眼部表现可以作为全身感染(包括 登革病毒)的早期诊断线索。它强调了多学科方法在管理这些感染方面的重要性,眼科医生在优化视觉和整体健康结果方面发挥着关键作用。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述指出,虽然已经认识到全身感染涉及眼部,但 登革病毒 中这种涉及的确切机制和程度仍不清楚。它还提到,眼科医生在处理这些感染中的作用尚未普遍标准化,这表明证据存在差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,需要进一步研究来阐明 登革病毒 眼部受累的机制,并规范眼科医生在其治疗中的作用。它还意味着需要改进 监测 和诊断策略,以更好地识别和解决与 监测 相关的眼部并发症。

title: A hierarchical clock-mixture model for Bayesian phylogenetic dating
abstract: Conditioning the inference of a Bayesian phylogenetic time tree on a single molecular clock model treats clock choice as fixed, even when support among plausible clock families is uncertain. When that assumption is wrong, estimated timescales and their uncertainty can be distorted. Existing practice usually addresses this by fitting strict, uncorrelated lognormal relaxed (UCLN), and autocorrelated clocks separately and comparing their marginal likelihoods, but this requires multiple computationally expensive model selection analyses.Here we introduce a hierarchical clock-mixture framework, implemented as the open-source \texttt{RelaxClockAveraging} package for BEAST~2, that separates two questions that are often conflated in clock comparison: whether branch-specific rate variation is needed at all, and, if it is, whether that variation is better described as uncorrelated or autocorrelated. The method averages analytically between strict and relaxed clocks at the top level and then compares UCLN and autocorrelated models within the relaxed class on a shared branch-rate vector, returning posterior probabilities for all three clock families together with model-averaged summaries for parameters shared across them. In stratified simulations, the generating clock family was retained in the 95\% posterior model set in all replicates, while model-averaged estimates of the overall substitution rate, root age, and tree length remained accurate. On a DENV-4 benchmark, the mixture reproduced the higher-effort nested-sampling ranking of clock families while avoiding the extreme run-to-run variability of independent marginal-likelihood estimates. On empirical benchmarks, the method recovered strong support for the autocorrelated clock on the classical 31-taxon chloroplast \textit{rbcL} data set. On an RSV-A G-gene data set it concentrated virtually all posterior support on UCLN while preserving the established RSV-A timescale. On a 245-taxon structured-coalescent H3N2 dataset it assigned most posterior mass to the relaxed-clock class, with support within that class concentrated on the autocorrelated family, and the inferred timescale remained consistent with the published estimate. These results show that clock-model support and downstream timescale sensitivity are related but not identical. Single-clock dating analyses can still be adequate, but fixing a clock model should be justified by posterior support rather than treated as a default assumption.

Existing practice usually addresses this by fitting strict, uncorrelated lognormal relaxed (UCLN), and autocorrelated clocks separately and comparing their marginal likelihoods, but this requires multiple computationally expensive model selection analyses.Here we introduce a hierarchical clock-mixture framework, implemented as the open-source \texttt{RelaxClockAveraging} package for BEAST~2, that separates two questions that are often conflated in clock comparison: whether branch-specific rate variation is needed at all, and, if it is, whether that variation is better described as uncorrelated or autocorrelated. The method averages analytically between strict and relaxed clocks at the top level and then compares UCLN and autocorrelated models within the relaxed class on a shared branch-rate vector, returning posterior probabilities for all three clock families together with model-averaged summaries for parameters shared across them. In stratified simulations, the generating clock family was retained in the 95\% posterior model set in all replicates, while model-averaged estimates of the overall substitution rate, root age, and tree length remained accurate. On a DENV-4 benchmark, the mixture reproduced the higher-effort nested-sampling ranking of clock families while avoiding the extreme run-to-run variability of independent marginal-likelihood estimates. On empirical benchmarks, the method recovered strong support for the autocorrelated clock on the classical 31-taxon chloroplast \textit{rbcL} data set. On an RSV-A G-gene data set it concentrated virtually all posterior support on UCLN while preserving the established RSV-A timescale. On a 245-taxon structured-coalescent H3N2 dataset it assigned most posterior mass to the relaxed-clock class, with support within that class concentrated on the autocorrelated family, and the inferred timescale remained consistent with the published estimate. These results show that clock-model support and downstream timescale sensitivity are related but not identical. Single-clock dating analyses can still be adequate, but fixing a clock model should be justified by posterior support rather than treated as a default assumption.

abstract_zh: 在单一分子钟模型条件下推断贝叶斯系统发育时间树,将钟的选择视为固定的,即使在合理的钟家族之间的支持是不确定的。当该假设错误时,估计的时间尺度及其不确定性可能会被扭曲。现有的做法通常通过分别拟合严格、不相关对数正态松弛(UCLN)和自相关钟并比较它们的边际似然来解决这个问题,但这需要多次计算昂贵的模型选择分析。在这里,我们介绍了一个分层钟混合框架,作为 BEAST~2 的开源 \texttt{RelaxClockAveraging} 包实现,它分离了在钟比较中经常混淆的两个问题:是否根本需要分支特异性速率变化,以及如果需要,该变化是否更好地描述为不相关或自相关。该方法在顶层在严格钟和松弛钟之间进行解析平均,然后在松弛类别内共享的分支速率 媒介 上比较 UCLN 和自相关模型,返回所有三个钟家族的后验概率以及它们之间共享参数的模型平均汇总。在分层模拟中,生成的钟家族在所有重复中都被保留在 95\% 后验模型集中,而整体替换率、根年龄和树长的模型平均估计保持准确。在 DENV-4 基准测试中,该混合模型重现了钟家族的更高努力嵌套采样排名,同时避免了独立边际似然估计的极端运行间变异性。在经验基准测试中,该方法在经典的 31 个分类单元叶绿体 \textit{rbcL} 数据集上恢复了对自相关钟的强有力支持。在一个 RSV-A G 基因数据集上,它几乎将所有后验支持集中在 UCLN 上,同时保持了既定的 RSV-A 时间尺度。在一个包含 245 个分类单元的结构化合并 H3N2 数据集上,它将大部分后验质量分配给松弛钟类别,该类别内的支持集中在自相关家族上,推断的时间尺度与已发表的估计保持一致。这些结果表明,钟模型支持和下游时间尺度敏感性是相关但不相同的。单钟定年分析可能仍然足够,但固定钟模型应由后验支持证明,而不是被视为默认假设。

title: MicroRNA Regulation of Aedes aegypti Infected with Three Different Pathogens: The Role of aae-miR-375 in Targeting bre-4 to Modulate Mosquito Immunity.
abstract: Aedes aegypti is an important vector of human pathogens, including dengue and chikungunya viruses. We examined midgut miRNA expression changes in Ae. aegypti following infection with Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Beauveria bassiana. We identified 19 differentially expressed miRNAs in the midgut of fourth-instar larvae infected with E. coli, 42 in larvae infected with S. aureus, and 134 in adult mosquitoes. The highest number of differentially expressed miRNAs (160) was observed in mosquitoes infected with B. Among these, aae-miR-375 showed the most pronounced change, with nearly 96% downregulation after S. The interaction between aae-miR-375 and Ae-bre-4 was validated using dual-luciferase assays. These results indicate that different pathogens induce distinct midgut miRNA expression profiles in Ae. Furthermore, we identified Ae-bre-4 as a target of aae-miR-375, providing new insights into the pathogen-miRNA-mRNA interactions that underlie mosquito immune responses. Collectively, these findings improve our understanding of mosquito immunity and may inform future vector control strategies.

title: Exploitation of host U2AF1 and U2AF2 splicing factors facilitates mosquito-borne orthoflavivirus infection across species
abstract: Abstract To identify novel host factors essential for orthoflavivirus replication, we performed proteomic profiling of endoplasmic reticulum fractions isolated from cells infected with Dengue virus or Zika virus (ZIKV). Among the enriched proteins, the splicing factor U2AF2 and its heterodimeric partner U2AF1 were found to be critical for efficient viral infection, functioning at the viral protein synthesis stage. The arginine/serine-rich (RS) domain and the first zinc knuckle (Zn1) of U2AF1, as well as nearly all domains except the RS domain of U2AF2, were essential for their proviral function. Disruption of the U2AF1–U2AF2 interaction potently suppressed ZIKV infection. U2AF1 and U2AF2 partially localize to the cytoplasm, and notably, the cytoplasmic U2AF2 was predominantly a truncated form that was sufficient to support viral replication. Both U2AF1 and U2AF2 bind to viral RNA, with U2AF1 binding being dependent on U2AF2. Interestingly, trans-complementation of the Aedes aegypti homolog u2af38 into U2AF1-knockout cells restored ZIKV replication, whereas expressing u2af50 in U2AF2-knockdown cells did not. However, knockdown of either u2af38 or u2af50 significantly inhibited the flavivirus replication in mosquitoes. Together, these findings reveal that flaviviruses co-opt host splicing factors in both human cells and mosquitoes, underscoring a conserved cross-species mechanism of viral exploitation.

title: Comparison of Oviposition and Adult Trapping to Monitor wMel Introgression for Wolbachia-Based Vector Control.
abstract: Wolbachia introgression into Aedes aegypti (Ae. aegypti) mosquito populations is an effective strategy for preventing dengue and is currently under evaluation for WHO prequalification. The standard protocol for trials and deployments currently being conducted in Brazil by the World Mosquito Program (WMP) for long-term monitoring of Wolbachia introgression involves the use of BG-Sentinel traps (BG-traps; Biogents AG [Regensburg, Germany]), which are labor-intensive and costly. More affordable alternatives, such as oviposition traps (ovitraps), have been used in other settings; however, a comparison of the WMP protocol for Wolbachia surveillance has not been performed. As part of the EVITA dengue trial, Ae. aegypti eggs and adults were collected from 124 ovitraps and 237 BG-traps across 12 clusters in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, between March and May 2023. Eggs collected from ovitraps were reared to L3 and L4 larvae, and wMel Wolbachia was detected using quantitative polymerase chain reaction testing in larvae and adult mosquitoes from BG-traps. Mixed-effects models were used to compare cluster-level estimates of wMel introgression derived from ovitrap and BG-trap data over time. Among 3,675 larvae reared from ovitraps, wMel prevalence was 0.50 (95% CI: 0.48-0.51), whereas 1,244 adults from BG-traps had a prevalence of 0.45 (95% CI: 0.42-0.48). Cluster-level introgression estimates from larvae and adults were strongly correlated (Spearman's r = 0.70; P <0.001). Multivariate models incorporating current- and previous-month ovitrap data and mosquito abundance revealed strong agreement between ovitrap-based predictions and BG-trap estimates (rs ≥0.98). These findings reveal that ovitrap-based surveillance provides a low-resource, efficient, and precise alternative for monitoring Wolbachia introgression as interventions are scaled in high-burden dengue settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of oviposition traps (ovitraps) as an alternative to BG-Sentinel traps for monitoring Wolbachia introgression in Aedes aegypti mosquitoes in Belo Horizonte, Brazil. Eggs and adults were collected from 124 ovitraps and 237 BG-traps between March and May 2023. Quantitative polymerase chain reaction testing detected Wolbachia (wMel) in larvae and adult mosquitoes, with prevalence rates of 0.50 (95% CI: 0.48-0.51) in ovitraps and 0.45 (95% CI: 0.42-0.48) in BG-traps. Cluster-level estimates from both methods were strongly correlated (Spearman's r = 0.70; P <0.001), and multivariate models showed strong agreement between ovitrap-based predictions and BG-trap estimates (rs ≥0.98). The authors concluded that ovitrap-based surveillance offers a low-resource, efficient, and precise alternative for monitoring Wolbachia introgression in high-burden dengue settings. The study's findings are significant for improving surveillance methods but are limited to abstract-only evidence, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估监测埃及伊蚊沃尔巴克氏体渗入的替代方法,这是预防登革热的关键策略。背景强调基于沃尔巴克氏体的 媒介 控制是预防登革热的有效策略,目前正在接受世界卫生组织资格预审评估。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究于 2023 年 3 月至 5 月在巴西贝洛奥里藏特进行,涉及 12 个集群中的 124 个产卵诱集器和 237 个 BG 诱集器。从这些诱捕器中收集埃及伊蚊卵和成虫以评估沃尔巴克氏体渗入。
elements_zh.methods: 从产卵器收集的卵被培育成 L3 和 L4 幼虫,并使用定量聚合酶链反应测试在 BG 陷阱的幼虫和成蚊中检测到沃尔巴克氏体 (wMel)。混合效应模型用于比较从产卵器和 BG 陷阱数据随时间推移得出的 wMel 渗入的簇水平估计。
elements_zh.main_results: 在产卵器饲养的 3,675 只幼虫中,wMel 患病率 为 0.50(95% CI:0.48-0.51),而 BG 诱捕器饲养的 1,244 只成虫的 患病率 为 0.45(95% CI:0.42-0.48)。幼虫和成虫的簇级渗入估计值密切相关(Spearman's r = 0.70;P <0.001)。结合当前和上个月产卵器数据和蚊子丰度的多变量模型显示,基于产卵器的预测与 BG 陷阱估计值之间具有很强的一致性(rs ≥0.98)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,随着干预措施在高负担登革热环境中规模化,基于产卵器的 监测 为监测沃尔巴克氏体渗入提供了一种资源匮乏、高效且精确的替代方案。这是一个新颖的发现,因为它首次在 WMP 协议的背景下直接比较产卵陷阱和 BG 陷阱数据。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更具成本效益和可扩展的 监测 方法提供信息,用于监测登革热多发地区的沃尔巴克氏体渗入,支持 媒介 控制的公共卫生策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于抽象证据,结果基于集群级别的估计。证据强度中等,因为研究结果来自单次试验,可能无法推广到所有情况。

title: Door muggen overdraagbare virussen: een toenemende bedreiging voor de volksgezondheid
abstract: Mosquito-borne viruses: an increasing risk for European travelers and public health Mosquito-borne viral infections pose an increasing threat to public health, amplified by globalization and the advance of invasive mosquito species such as Aedes albopictus. International travel exposes travelers to a range of viruses, while endemic areas grapple with significant disease burden and socio-economic consequences. Japanese encephalitis, chikungunya, Zika, and dengue illustrate the diversity of this threat. This article is a narrative review based on the recent literature and epidemiological data. Japanese encephalitis, transmitted by Culex mosquitoes, causes severe neurological complications, particularly in Asia. Chikungunya, spread by Aedes mosquitoes, is characterized by prolonged joint pain. Zika, also transmitted by Aedes, is notorious for congenital abnormalities. Dengue, with 4 serotypes, has a global distribution and can lead to severe hemorrhagic fever. For none of these viral infections is there a specific antiviral treatment; the approach is mainly symptomatic. Climate change and the further spread of invasive mosquito species are expected to lead to an increase in outbreaks, both in frequency and geographical spread. Continuous monitoring, vector control, public education, and vaccination efforts are essential to address this growing threat.

title: Negative Binomial tv-DINGARCH Models for Monthly DHF Cases in Surabaya, Indonesia (2015-2025)
abstract: Count time series data are commonly encountered in epidemiological studies, such as monthly reports of Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) cases. The INGARCH model has been widely used to handle temporal dependence and overdispersion in such data. However, the standard INGARCH model assumes constant dispersion, whereas in practice the dispersion level may vary over time due to epidemiological factors like seasonality or vector control policies. Accurately capturing this time-varying variability is essential for reliable disease surveillance. This study applies the tv-DINGARCH model to DHF cases in Surabaya from January 2015 to December 2025. The tv-DINGARCH(1,1,1,1) model with Negative Binomial distribution is used because it allows the dispersion parameter \(\phi_t\) to evolve dynamically. Parameter estimation is conducted using the Conditional Maximum Likelihood Estimation method implemented in RStudio. The results show that the tv-DINGARCH model yields AIC = 968.43 and BIC = 985.68, both smaller than those of the standard INGARCH model (AIC = 1012.18, BIC = 1023.68). The likelihood ratio test produces an LR statistic of 47.7560 with a p-value less than 0.000001, strongly rejecting constant dispersion. The stationarity condition is satisfied with \(\beta_2 + \alpha_2 + \beta_1 + \alpha_1 = 0.9990 1\). From a public health perspective, these findings indicate that the tv-DINGARCH model better captures the fluctuating dynamics of DHF transmission, supporting more effective surveillance and early warning systems.

source_records.title: Negative Binomial tv-DINGARCH Models for Monthly DHF Cases in Surabaya, Indonesia (2015-2025)
source_records.abstract: Count time series data are commonly encountered in epidemiological studies, such as monthly reports of Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever (DHF) cases. The INGARCH model has been widely used to handle temporal dependence and overdispersion in such data. However, the standard INGARCH model assumes constant dispersion, whereas in practice the dispersion level may vary over time due to epidemiological factors like seasonality or vector control policies. Accurately capturing this time-varying variability is essential for reliable disease surveillance. This study applies the tv-DINGARCH model to DHF cases in Surabaya from January 2015 to December 2025. The tv-DINGARCH(1,1,1,1) model with Negative Binomial distribution is used because it allows the dispersion parameter \(\phi_t\) to evolve dynamically. Parameter estimation is conducted using the Conditional Maximum Likelihood Estimation method implemented in RStudio. The results show that the tv-DINGARCH model yields AIC = 968.43 and BIC = 985.68, both smaller than those of the standard INGARCH model (AIC = 1012.18, BIC = 1023.68). The likelihood ratio test produces an LR statistic of 47.7560 with a p-value less than 0.000001, strongly rejecting constant dispersion. The stationarity condition is satisfied with \(\beta_2 + \alpha_2 + \beta_1 + \alpha_1 = 0.9990 1\). From a public health perspective, these findings indicate that the tv-DINGARCH model better captures the fluctuating dynamics of DHF transmission, supporting more effective surveillance and early warning systems.

title: Technological Innovations in Vector-Borne Disease Control and Their Relationship with Public Health
abstract: Background: Diseases transmitted by vectors remain a major challenge to public health in Indonesia. Continuous use of chemical insecticides has led to resistance, while climate change and vector behavior further exacerbate disease transmission. Therefore, innovative, effective, and sustainable technologies are needed to support community-based vector control efforts. Objective: To review various technological innovations in vector-borne disease control and their relationship with improving public health based on literature from the past five years. Methods: This study is a literature review employing a systematic and narrative approach. The search was conducted through the PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, Garuda, and Indonesia OneSearch databases using the keywords “vector control technology innovation” and “public health.” Articles included were publications from 2020–2025 that were relevant to the topic. Results: From the 20 selected articles, five major innovations were identified: the Wolbachia technique, Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) and gene drive, autodissemination using pyriproxyfen, plant-based biolarvicides utilizing local resources, and digital systems based on IoT and GIS. These innovations have been shown to reduce vector density and the incidence of diseases such as dengue and malaria, as well as enhance community participation. Conclusion: Innovative technologies have proven to be more environmentally friendly and efficient compared to conventional methods. Their successful implementation requires policy support, infrastructure readiness, and cross-sector collaboration within the framework of Integrated Vector Management (IVM). Keywords: Technological innovation, vector control, public health, Wolbachia, autodissemination.
